chapters.title: Preface: Why This Book Is Being Given Away
The Definition of Constitutional Capitalism
chapters.summary: Present the approved definition, explain each clause, and show why free enterprise and constitutional accountability are jointly necessary.
chapters.central_question: What precisely is Constitutional Capitalism, and how does the canonical definition govern the book?
research_requirements: Uses of “constitutional” as applied to economic power

chapters.title: The Central Proposition
chapters.summary: Develop the central belief that prosperity must serve a free and self-governing people, not merely aggregate wealth.
chapters.central_question: What is the book’s governing proposition about the purpose of an economy?

chapters.title: The Concentration of Wealth and Power
What Happened to the Common Worker?
When Communities Lose Their Economic Center
The Purpose of an Economy
chapters.summary: Establish evaluative criteria: dignity, liberty, security, opportunity, family, community, self-government, and intergenerational progress.

chapters.title: The Dignity of Work
chapters.summary: Work is contribution and a path toward independence; productivity gains should not flow exclusively upward; human worth is not reducible to employment.
chapters.central_question: How should a free republic understand work?
research_requirements: Labor share / productivity debates (for later sourcing)

chapters.title: The Responsibilities of Ownership
chapters.summary: Ownership rights remain; responsibilities include bearing risk, avoiding monopoly abuse, and honoring obligations attached to legal privilege.
chapters.central_question: What responsibilities accompany ownership and investment?
research_requirements: Corporate charter history; limited liability duties

chapters.title: Competition Protects Liberty
chapters.summary: Competition disperses power, protects choice, strengthens bargaining, and limits political capture; antitrust is part of republican architecture.
chapters.central_question: Why is competition a constitutional safeguard?
research_requirements: Antitrust and republican government literature queue

chapters.title: Power Naturally Concentrates
chapters.summary: Without rules protecting rivalry and accountability, power gathers in markets as in politics; both public and private concentration threaten liberty.
chapters.central_question: Why does economic power concentrate, and why does that matter constitutionally?

chapters.title: Government Must Be Limited and Capable
chapters.summary: Government must be limited in scope and capable in legitimate functions: enforce contracts, protect property, defend competition, prevent capture — without commanding ordinary production.
chapters.central_question: What is the proper character of government in Constitutional Capitalism?

chapters.title: Ownership Is the Foundation of Economic Freedom
chapters.summary: Wages support life; ownership builds independence. Broad ownership is the primary mechanism for durable prosperity and distributed influence.
chapters.central_question: Why is broad ownership central rather than optional?

Article III: The Rights and Duties of Owners

chapters.summary: Translate Declaration principles into an Article-level statement of government duties and prohibitions without claiming finished legal text.
chapters.central_question: How should the Economic Articles define government’s role?

Taxing Wealth Creation Without Taxing Survival
Moving the Burden Away from Ordinary Work
Profit Sharing as an Economic Right
Labor, Benefits, and the Future of Work
Housing and the Geography of Opportunity
Energy, Natural Resources, and Economic Rents
A New Measure of National Prosperity
When Economic Power Becomes Political Power
Information Power, Media, and Digital Platforms
The Balance Between National Standards and Local Control
Reform Without Revolution
chapters.summary: Reject confiscatory chaos and class retaliation; require law, consent, prospective rules, phased implementation, measurement, and correction.
chapters.central_question: How can deep economic reform proceed without destroying productive order?
research_requirements: Transition failures and successful gradual reforms

chapters.title: What Must Change First
chapters.summary: Define a First 100 Days / early sequencing agenda: which laws are introduced, which agencies change, what stays the same, and what protections exist. Prefer structural setup over dramatic overnight redistribution.
chapters.central_question: What should happen first — and what should remain unchanged — in the opening phase of reform?

chapters.title: A Ten-Year Transition Framework
chapters.summary: Develop scenario horizons (years 1–3, 3–7, 7–15, 10–20) as predictions, not promises. Emphasize that isolated policies differ from system-level reform; ownership broadening is the distinctive long-horizon mechanism.
chapters.central_question: How could a 10–20 year transition unfold if Constitutional Capitalism were implemented as a system?

chapters.title: Protecting Small Businesses During the Transition
International Adoption and National Adaptation
chapters.summary: Universal principles of enterprise-plus-accountability can travel; statutory design must adapt to constitutional structure and local institutions.
chapters.central_question: Which principles are universal, and which designs must vary by nation?

chapters.title: Testing, Measurement, and Constitutional Review
chapters.summary: Specify a testing ladder: models → state pilots → regional implementation → national adoption. Pre-define metrics, publish failures, and require periodic constitutional-style review (living framework).
chapters.central_question: How would Constitutional Capitalism be tested, measured, and revised?

chapters.title: How Constitutional Capitalism Can Fail
chapters.summary: Steelman failure modes: investment decline, capital flight, price increases, ownership stagnation, bureaucratic burden, and shifted capture. Define detection metrics and adjustment paths. Title spirit: If We Are Wrong.
chapters.central_question: How could Constitutional Capitalism fail, and how would we know?

chapters.title: The Family in a Prosperous Republic
A New Social Compact Without Centralized Control
What We Owe the Next Generation
The Prosperous, Free, and Self-Governing People
The Declaration of Constitutional Capitalism
chapters.summary: Publish and refine the standalone Declaration as the philosophical spine for principles, articles, and policies.
chapters.central_question: What founding statement should govern the project?
